items.title: NEW — `Owner` has no DISPOSED state: `dispose` runs and empties its cleanups but keeps no flag, so a `take`/`defer` that lands AFTER disposal (an async continuation whose scope was torn down first — a route switched away before a handle's reply) sits on a list nothing runs again: the subscription fires for the rest of the session and only a SECOND `dispose` releases it. Probed: an `effect` registered from a continuation after `owner.dispose()` fires on every later `set`; a remote mirror leased this way stays subscribed (count never returns to 0, the server forwards forever) — kolt's channel switch before the channel's first reply is exactly this shape
items.discussion: found investigating kolt's quick-switch freeze report (2026-09-11; the freeze itself not reproduced headless); scratchpad `kolt-markers/pa7` is the pin; sibling of B283 (a release hook resolving its creation turn) — both are 'ambient capture outlives the extent'
items.body: A `disposed: Shared<bool>` on `Owner`; `take`/`defer` on a disposed owner run the cleanup IMMEDIATELY (the item is disposed on the spot, the deferred action runs now) instead of parking it; `dispose` is idempotent. Pins: the late `effect` never fires after the owner went; a `RemoteSource` lease taken from a continuation after disposal sends `Subscribe` and then its `Unsubscribe` in the same segment (or, better, never subscribes — `acquire` on a disposed ambient owner is a no-op lease); `bind_each`/`swap` boundaries unchanged. Consider a debug assertion under the LSP/dev build naming the site that registered late.
